payload.goal:
Add exactly 4 independent warehouse analytics modules to the verified W1 codebase.
Create src/analytics/contracts.ts exporting WarehouseProjection with a readonly id and project(scenario), where project returns the answer to that module's question.
Each module answers one question, computed from the W1 Scenario, layout and inventory exports:
- src/analytics/projection-01.ts exports the projection "zone-unit-totals": Total units stored in each zone, keyed by zone id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-01.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-02.ts exports the projection "sku-unit-totals": Total units of each SKU across the whole warehouse, keyed by SKU id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-02.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-03.ts exports the projection "bin-occupancy": How many bins hold stock, how many are empty, and how many exist. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-03.test.ts.
- src/analytics/projection-04.ts exports the projection "sku-bin-spread": Number of distinct bins each SKU occupies, keyed by SKU id. Its focused tests live in src/analytics/projection-04.test.ts.
A module must not import another module; it may import only the fixed contract and W1 exports.
Every answer must be derived from the scenario at run time. Do not hardcode results, and do not duplicate the W1 inventory or layout calculations.
Create src/analytics/registry.ts as the sole consumer of every module, returning all projections in the order the modules are listed above, with its own tests in src/analytics/registry.test.ts.
Preserve all existing W1 behaviour and checks.
Add a package script named study:wide-graph that writes exactly one JSON object to stdout and no other output.
Its JSON must be { "schemaVersion": 1, "moduleCount": 4, "scenario": "thesis-seed-2026", "projections": [ { "projectionId": "<the module's projection id>", "value": <that module's answer> }, … ] } with exactly 4 entries in the order the modules are listed above.
Two invocations from the same commit must emit byte-identical JSON.

root.title: Warehouse analytics W1 projections
root.objective: Add four independent runtime analytics projections over the verified W1 scenario and expose deterministic study output without changing existing W1 behavior.
expectedOutcomes: Four projection modules compute their answers from the W1 scenario at run time.
Projection modules share only the analytics contract and W1 exports, not each other.
The registry is the sole in-repo consumer of every projection module and returns them in required order.
study:wide-graph emits one byte-stable JSON object with four ordered projection results.
Existing W1 domain, scenario and probe checks remain covered.

complexitySignals.rationale: The change spans a new analytics folder, existing W1 domain/scenario exports, and package scripts, but keeps public surface narrow.

cut.rationale: The contract, four independent projections, registry ordering, and command output each have distinct observable acceptance checks; keeping projections separate also enforces the no-cross-import requirement.

children.title: Analytics projection contract
children.objective: Create the shared WarehouseProjection contract used by analytics modules and the registry.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/contracts.ts exports WarehouseProjection.
WarehouseProjection has a readonly id and project(scenario).
The contract references the existing W1 scenario type rather than inventing a parallel scenario shape.

complexitySignals.rationale: Small file, but it is the exported type contract all analytics units depend on.

children.title: Zone unit totals projection
children.objective: Implement and test the zone-unit-totals projection from W1 scenario layout and inventory data.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-01.ts exports a projection with id zone-unit-totals.
project(scenario) returns total units stored in each zone keyed by zone id.
The implementation imports only src/analytics/contracts.ts and W1 exports.
src/analytics/projection-01.test.ts verifies the focused answer and guards against static or unrelated behavior.

complexitySignals.rationale: Requires understanding how W1 inventory locations map through layout zones and validating the aggregate.

children.title: SKU unit totals projection
children.objective: Implement and test the sku-unit-totals projection from W1 scenario inventory data.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-02.ts exports a projection with id sku-unit-totals.
project(scenario) returns total units of each SKU across the whole warehouse keyed by SKU id.
The implementation imports only src/analytics/contracts.ts and W1 exports.
src/analytics/projection-02.test.ts verifies the focused answer.

complexitySignals.rationale: Narrow aggregate over inventory quantities with focused scenario-based validation.

children.title: Bin occupancy projection
children.objective: Implement and test the bin-occupancy projection from W1 scenario layout and inventory data.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-03.ts exports a projection with id bin-occupancy.
project(scenario) returns how many bins hold stock, how many are empty, and how many exist.
Existing layout exports are used to count bins; existing inventory exports are used to determine occupied bins.
The implementation imports only src/analytics/contracts.ts and W1 exports.
src/analytics/projection-03.test.ts verifies occupied, empty, and total counts.

complexitySignals.rationale: Combines layout bin cardinality with inventory occupancy, so both W1 domains must be understood.

children.title: SKU bin spread projection
children.objective: Implement and test the sku-bin-spread projection from W1 scenario inventory data.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/projection-04.ts exports a projection with id sku-bin-spread.
project(scenario) returns the number of distinct bins each SKU occupies keyed by SKU id.
The implementation imports only src/analytics/contracts.ts and W1 exports.
src/analytics/projection-04.test.ts verifies distinct-bin counting and avoids counting repeated stock entries in the same bin twice if the W1 model permits them.

complexitySignals.rationale: Distinct-bin semantics add a small edge-case validation surface beyond simple summing.

children.title: Analytics projection registry
children.objective: Create the sole registry consumer of all four projections and verify ordering and membership.
expectedOutcomes: src/analytics/registry.ts imports all four projection modules and returns all projections in the listed order.
No other new unit imports projection modules directly except tests focused on their owning module and the study output implementation through the registry.
src/analytics/registry.test.ts verifies module count, ids, and order.

complexitySignals.rationale: The registry is a small integration point whose correctness depends on exact module membership and order.
